title: Base change maps of modules compose along horizontally pasted squares
statement:
For a commutative square of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] $f\circ v=u\circ f_1$, with $f:X\to S$, $u:T\to S$, $f_1:X_1\to T$, $v:X_1\to X$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the *base change map* $\beta_{\mathcal F}:u^*f_*\mathcal F\to f_{1*}v^*\mathcal F$ of the square is the morphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules corresponding, under the adjunction $u^*\dashv u_*$ of pullback and pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], to $f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F}):f_*\mathcal F\to f_*v_*v^*\mathcal F=u_*f_{1*}v^*\mathcal F$, where $\eta_v$ is the unit of $v^*\dashv v_*$ and the equality holds because both sheaves have the sections $(v^*\mathcal F)(v^{-1}f^{-1}W)=(v^*\mathcal F)(f_1^{-1}u^{-1}W)$ over an open $W\subseteq S$; $\beta$ is natural in $\mathcal F$. For morphisms of schemes $a:Z\to Y$, $b:Y\to W$ let $c_{b,a}:a^*b^*\xrightarrow{\sim}(b\circ a)^*$ be the composition isomorphism of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], the unique isomorphism with $(b\circ a)_*(c_{b,a})\circ b_*(\eta_{a,b^*})\circ\eta_b=\eta_{b\circ a}$ (conjugate to the equality $(b\circ a)_*=b_*a_*$). Let $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$, $f'':X''\to S''$, $g:S'\to S$, $g':X'\to X$, $h:S''\to S'$, $h':X''\to X'$ be morphisms of schemes with $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ and $f'\circ h'=h\circ f''$, so that $f\circ(g'\circ h')=(g\circ h)\circ f''$; let $\beta^{1}$, $\beta^{2}$, $\beta^{12}$ be the base change maps of the squares $(f,f',g,g')$, $(f',f'',h,h')$ and of the outer rectangle $(f,f'',g\circ h,g'\circ h')$. Then for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$
$$\beta^{12}_{\mathcal F}=f''_*(c_{g',h',\mathcal F})\circ\beta^{2}_{g'^*\mathcal F}\circ h^*(\beta^{1}_{\mathcal F})\circ c_{g,h,f_*\mathcal F}^{-1}:$$
$$(g h)^*f_*\mathcal F\to h^*g^*f_*\mathcal F\to h^*f'_*g'^*\mathcal F\to f''_*h'^*g'^*\mathcal F\to f''_*(g'h')^*\mathcal F.$$

proof.text: *(1) Conventions.* For a morphism of schemes $k:Y\to Z$ [def-pc-scheme], the adjunction $k^*\dashv k_*$ of pullback and pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] (Stacks, Sheaves, Lemma 0096), with unit $\eta_k$, gives the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(k^*\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal M,k_*\mathcal N)$, $\psi\mapsto k_*(\psi)\circ\eta_{k,\mathcal M}$, for $\mathcal O_Z$-modules $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal N$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; it is the morphism *corresponding* to $\psi$ in the statement. In particular two morphisms $\psi_1,\psi_2:k^*\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ are equal as soon as $k_*(\psi_1)\circ\eta_{k,\mathcal M}=k_*(\psi_2)\circ\eta_{k,\mathcal M}$, and every $\phi:\mathcal M\to k_*\mathcal N$ is $k_*(\psi)\circ\eta_{k,\mathcal M}$ for exactly one $\psi$. The unit is natural: $k_*k^*(\phi)\circ\eta_{k,\mathcal M}=\eta_{k,\mathcal M'}\circ\phi$ for $\phi:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$. Pushforward is computed on sections, $(k_*\mathcal N)(W)=\mathcal N(k^{-1}W)$ and $k_*(\psi)_W=\psi_{k^{-1}W}$; hence for morphisms $a:Z'\to Y$, $b:Y\to W$ the functors $(b\circ a)_*$ and $b_*\circ a_*$ from $\mathcal O_{Z'}$-modules to $\mathcal O_W$-modules are equal (Stacks, Sheaves, Lemma 0097): same sections $\mathcal N(a^{-1}b^{-1}V)$, same maps, and the same $\mathcal O_W$-module structure because $(b\circ a)^\sharp=b_*(a^\sharp)\circ b^\sharp$ (Stacks, Sheaves, Definition 0093). Consequently, for a commutative square $f\circ v=u\circ f_1$ as in the statement, $f_*v_*=(f\circ v)_*=(u\circ f_1)_*=u_*f_{1*}$. For the rectangle of the statement this gives the equalities of functors $(g\circ h)_*=g_*h_*$, $(g'\circ h')_*=g'_*h'_*$, $g_*f'_*=f_*g'_*$, $h_*f''_*=f'_*h'_*$, and hence $(g\circ h)_*f''_*=g_*h_*f''_*=g_*f'_*h'_*=f_*g'_*h'_*=f_*(g'\circ h')_*$; these identifications are used without comment below. All of this is the definition of an adjunction and of pushforward.

proof.text: *(2) The base change map is well defined and natural.* For the square $f\circ v=u\circ f_1$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, $f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F}):f_*\mathcal F\to f_*v_*v^*\mathcal F=u_*f_{1*}v^*\mathcal F$ (step (1)) is a morphism of $\mathcal O_S$-modules, so by step (1) there is exactly one $\beta_{\mathcal F}:u^*f_*\mathcal F\to f_{1*}v^*\mathcal F$ with $$u_*(\beta_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{u,f_*\mathcal F}=f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F}).\qquad(\ast)$$ Naturality: for $\phi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ the two morphisms $\beta_{\mathcal F'}\circ u^*f_*(\phi)$ and $f_{1*}v^*(\phi)\circ\beta_{\mathcal F}$ from $u^*f_*\mathcal F$ to $f_{1*}v^*\mathcal F'$ have the adjoints $u_*(\beta_{\mathcal F'})\circ\eta_{u,f_*\mathcal F'}\circ f_*(\phi)=f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F'}\circ\phi)$ (naturality of $\eta_u$ and $(\ast)$) and $u_*f_{1*}v^*(\phi)\circ f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F})=f_*(v_*v^*(\phi)\circ\eta_{v,\mathcal F})=f_*(\eta_{v,\mathcal F'}\circ\phi)$ ($(\ast)$, $u_*f_{1*}=f_*v_*$ and naturality of $\eta_v$), which agree; so they are equal by step (1).

proof.text: *(3) The composition isomorphisms $c_{b,a}$ exist and are unique.* Let $a:Z\to Y$, $b:Y\to W$ be morphisms of schemes. Composing the adjunctions $b^*\dashv b_*$ and $a^*\dashv a_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] gives the composite adjunction $a^*b^*\dashv b_*a_*$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] (with $F=b^*$, $G=b_*$, $H=a^*$, $I=a_*$) with unit $b_*(\eta_{a,b^*\mathcal M})\circ\eta_{b,\mathcal M}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $L_1=a^*b^*\dashv R_1=b_*a_*$ (this unit), $L_2=(b\circ a)^*\dashv R_2=(b\circ a)_*$ (unit $\eta_{b\circ a}$) and $\delta=\mathrm{id}:R_2=(b\circ a)_*\to b_*a_*=R_1$ (the equality of step (1)): there is a unique natural transformation $c_{b,a}:a^*b^*\to(b\circ a)^*$ with $b_*a_*(c_{b,a,\mathcal M})\circ b_*(\eta_{a,b^*\mathcal M})\circ\eta_{b,\mathcal M}=\eta_{b\circ a,\mathcal M}$ for every $\mathcal O_W$-module $\mathcal M$, i.e. $(b\circ a)_*(c_{b,a})\circ b_*(\eta_{a,b^*})\circ\eta_b=\eta_{b\circ a}$, and it is an isomorphism; uniqueness among isomorphisms follows from uniqueness among all natural transformations. This is the isomorphism $(b\circ a)^*\cong a^*b^*$ of Stacks, Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (obtained there from $(b\circ a)_*=b_*a_*$ by uniqueness of adjoints), normalised by its compatibility with the units (Stacks, Categories, Lemma 0B65), so the composition isomorphisms in the statement are well defined.

proof.text:
*(4) The pasting identity.* Fix an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, put $\mathcal M=f_*\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G=g'^*\mathcal F$, $c=c_{g,h}$, $c'=c_{g',h'}$ (step (3)), and let $ho=f''_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ eta^2_{\mathcal G}\circ h^*( eta^1_{\mathcal F})\circ c^{-1}_{\mathcal M}:(g\circ h)^*\mathcal M	o f''_*(g'\circ h')^*\mathcal F$ be the right-hand side. By step (2) for the outer rectangle, $ eta^{12}_{\mathcal F}$ is the unique morphism whose adjoint under $(g\circ h)^*\dashv(g\circ h)_*$ is $f_*(\eta_{g'\circ h',\mathcal F})$; so by step (1) it suffices to show $(g\circ h)_*(ho)\circ\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}=f_*(\eta_{g'\circ h',\mathcal F})$ as maps $\mathcal M	o(g\circ h)_*f''_*(g'\circ h')^*\mathcal F=f_*(g'\circ h')_*(g'\circ h')^*\mathcal F$. Write $\sigma=f''_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ eta^2_{\mathcal G}\circ h^*( eta^1_{\mathcal F}):h^*g^*\mathcal M	o f''_*(g'\circ h')^*\mathcal F$, so $ho=\sigma\circ c^{-1}_{\mathcal M}$.
(a) The defining equation of $c$ at $\mathcal M$ (step (3), $b=g$, $a=h$) reads $(g\circ h)_*(c_{\mathcal M})\circ g_*(\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M})\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal M}=\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}$; applying $(g\circ h)_*(c^{-1}_{\mathcal M})$ gives $(g\circ h)_*(c^{-1}_{\mathcal M})\circ\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}=g_*(\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M})\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal M}$. Hence $(g\circ h)_*(ho)\circ\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}=g_* ig(h_*(\sigma)\circ\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M} ig)\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal M}$, using $(g\circ h)_*=g_*h_*$.
(b) Naturality of $\eta_h$ for $ eta^1_{\mathcal F}:g^*\mathcal M	o f'_*\mathcal G$ gives $h_*h^*( eta^1_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M}=\eta_{h,f'_*\mathcal G}\circ eta^1_{\mathcal F}$, so $h_*(\sigma)\circ\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M}=h_*f''_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ h_*( eta^2_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{h,f'_*\mathcal G}\circ eta^1_{\mathcal F}$.
(c) Equation $(\ast)$ of step (2) for the square $(f',f'',h,h')$ at $\mathcal G$ is $h_*( eta^2_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{h,f'_*\mathcal G}=f'_*(\eta_{h',\mathcal G})$; with $h_*f''_*=f'_*h'_*$ this gives $h_*(\sigma)\circ\eta_{h,g^*\mathcal M}=f'_* ig(h'_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{h',\mathcal G} ig)\circ eta^1_{\mathcal F}$.
(d) Inserting (c) into (a) and using $(\ast)$ for the square $(f,f',g,g')$ at $\mathcal F$, $g_*( eta^1_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{g,\mathcal M}=f_*(\eta_{g',\mathcal F})$, together with $g_*f'_*=f_*g'_*$: $(g\circ h)_*(ho)\circ\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}=f_*g'_* ig(h'_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{h',\mathcal G} ig)\circ f_*(\eta_{g',\mathcal F})=f_* ig(g'_*h'_*(c'_{\mathcal F})\circ g'_*(\eta_{h',g'^*\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{g',\mathcal F} ig)$.
(e) The defining equation of $c'$ at $\mathcal F$ (step (3), $b=g'$, $a=h'$, $(g'\circ h')_*=g'_*h'_*$) says that the bracket equals $\eta_{g'\circ h',\mathcal F}$. So $(g\circ h)_*(ho)\circ\eta_{g\circ h,\mathcal M}=f_*(\eta_{g'\circ h',\mathcal F})$, and $ho= eta^{12}_{\mathcal F}$ by step (1). (This is the instance, for pullback and pushforward of modules, of the compatibility of mates with pasting of squares and with change of the adjunction along conjugate transformations; for the derived functors it is Stacks, Cohomology, Remark 0ATM, whose verification is omitted there.)

Agent-written (Stacks 0ATM omits the verification), four steps, no new node: adjunction conventions (0096, 0097, 0093), beta well defined and natural, the composition isomorphisms c_{b,a} from the composite-adjunction leaf and the conjugate-isomorphism leaf (both Mathlib), the pasting identity by a chase of adjoints and units. Stage-3 notes: the sibling lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-algebra cites 008Z where 0096 is the right lemma; def-pc-module-pullback gives (h o g)^* = g^* h^* with no normalisation, which this item fixes by the unit equation and other nodes assume silently. split_report.summary: Split in four steps, no new node. Step 1 fixes the adjunction conventions as in the sibling lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-algebra (hom bijection psi -> k_*(psi) o eta_k, naturality of units, (b o a)_* = b_* a_* on sections, Stacks 0096, 0097, 0093). Step 2 proves the claims inside the statement about beta: it is well defined (unique adjoint of f_*(eta_v)) and natural in F (adjoints compared). Step 3 proves that the composition isomorphisms c_{b,a} of the statement exist, are unique and invertible, from the composite adjunction a^*b^* -| b_*a_* (Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction) and the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation with delta = id, exactly as lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition does for etale sheaves; def-pc-module-pullback only asserts (h o g)^* = g^*h^* without normalisation, so the statement's own unit characterisation is what is used. Step 4 is the diagram chase: the adjoint of the right-hand side under (gh)^* -| (gh)_* is computed with the defining equation of c_{g,h}, naturality of eta_h, the defining equations (*) of beta^2 and beta^1, and the defining equation of c_{g',h'}, and comes out as f_*(eta_{g'h'}), the adjoint of beta^{12}. Stacks Remark 0ATM (derived, verification omitted) checked: tag and label correct; the base change map of Remark 08HY is defined through the adjunction f'^* -| f'_* rather than g^* -| g_*, but the node defines beta through g^* -| g_* (as Cohomology Section 02N6 does in degree 0), and nothing here needs the comparison. The proof is agent-written.
